For the reaction γ  +  γCMB  →  e⁺e⁻ the squared centre–of–mass energy is  

s = 2 E ε (1 − cos θ),

where E is the energy of the high–energy γ-ray, ε the energy of the CMB photon and θ the angle between their momenta.  
The smallest E required is obtained for a head–on collision (θ = π, 1 − cos θ = 2):

s = 4 E ε.

Pair production becomes possible when s reaches (2 mₑc²)²:

4 E ε = (2 mₑc²)²  ⇒  E = (mₑc²)² / ε.

Insert the numbers  

mₑc² ≃ 0.511 MeV = 5.11 × 10⁵ eV  
ε (average CMB photon) ≃ 1 × 10⁻³ eV.

E = (5.11 × 10⁵ eV)² / (1 × 10⁻³ eV)  
  = 2.6 × 10¹¹ eV² / 1 × 10⁻³ eV  
  = 2.6 × 10¹⁴ eV  
  = 2.6 × 10⁵ GeV.

Therefore γ-rays with energies above about 2.6 × 10⁵ GeV will have their lifetimes limited by annihilation with CMB photons.

Answer: B
